name: FFmpeg / ffprobe
role: Native encoding, muxing, filtergraphs, probing and sequence assembly; every renderer's delivery path
summary: The command-line media toolchain. Every renderer's output becomes video here: image sequences to H.264, VP9 or ProRes 4444 with alpha, audio muxing, overlays and crossfades in filtergraphs, trims and concatenation, and ffprobe as the inspection tool the examples diff against. Deterministic in metadata and frames per build, not in container bytes.
use_when: Any encode, mux, trim, concatenate or probe
Assembling an image sequence from any renderer into a deliverable
Overlaying flat layers with alpha before VCR's compositor exists
Verifying a render: frame count, fps, duration, pixel format
avoid_when: Editorial decisions: those belong in VCR's timeline, FFmpeg gets resolved intervals
In-browser conversion with no native binary: Mediabunny or ffmpeg.wasm
Shot detection or scene splitting: PySceneDetect drives FFmpeg for you
GIF quality matters: encode frames with gifski

facets.one_line: Codecs and pixel formats for web, alpha and intermediate delivery
Combine audio and video, concatenate, who is authoritative on duration
Overlay with alpha, crossfade, scale and colour range
ffprobe JSON as evidence and as a test oracle
Sequence clocks, holds, gaps and rounding

license: LGPL-2.1 or GPL depending on build flags
notes: Delivery path for every renderer; first FFmpeg assembly example planned in M0.

evidence.result: 48 frames at 24 fps mux to 2.000000 s with AAC; ffprobe JSON matches expected/

48 frames at 24 fps (h264 320x180) muxed with a 2 s 440 Hz AAC tone using -shortest; probed duration 2.000000 s, 95 AAC frames at 48 kHz; streams and format match expected/ffprobe.json. Env: Linux x86_64 container, ImageMagick 6.9.12-98 via convert shim.
evidence.scope: PNG sequence plus generated tone muxed to H.264/AAC MP4 on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu FFmpeg 6.1.1 build); media facts compared, not ffprobe JSON layout.
